slides.title: Exploring Space
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 2: Exploring Space. Unit 2 pairs two information texts about astronomy and life on the space station with The Burrow Discovery, a story about a school science fair. You will study twenty-five words such as burrow, boycott, glare, cooperate and ownership, and you will master indefinite pronouns, singular agreement and adverbial phrases. You will separate fact from opinion, compare biography with autobiography, and write a friendly blog post of your own. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Use the twenty-five Unit 2 words about science, systems and social values accurately in speech and writing.
Identify indefinite pronouns in a text and use them with the matching singular or plural verb.
Read an information text about astronomy and extract main points supported by evidence.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to use the twenty-five Unit 2 words about science, systems and social values accurately in speech and writing. You will also identify indefinite pronouns in a text and use them with the matching singular or plural verb. You will also read an information text about astronomy and extract main points supported by evidence. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: independence, issue, empire, expose, glare, source. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Night Sky Above Us and Life on the Space Station. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Indefinite pronouns: talking about people and things in general
bullets: Indefinite pronouns stand in for people or things when we do not need to name them exactly. One short word can replace a whole list, which keeps writing...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Indefinite pronouns: talking about people and things in general. Indefinite pronouns stand in for people or things when we do not need to name them exactly. One short word can replace a whole list, which keeps writing smooth and clear. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1: A space discovery blog post
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Astronaut interview role-play. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
